title: Scale- and reliability-aware task relation literature gate
hypothesis: At least one published explicit Task Relation Learning method models unequal task scale or reliability, maps directly to F9, and is faithfully implementable for heterogeneous deep classification without category drift.
outcome: No reviewed method satisfied all eligibility gates. Explicit relation models did not directly regulate heterogeneous deep shared-gradient scale; direct scale-balancing methods did not learn task relations; the recent informative-relation model crossed the decomposition boundary.

closest_candidate.positive: Separates signal task covariance from residual/noise task covariance.
closest_candidate.blocking_mismatch: Fully observed aligned Gaussian multi-output regression; no faithful heterogeneous multiclass deep-classification adaptation and no direct gradient-scale mechanism.

direct_symptom_method.positive: Directly balances dominant task gradient magnitudes.
direct_symptom_method.blocking_mismatch: Learns per-task loss weights, not task relations; optimization category outside formal scope.

framework_update: Relation magnitude, relation confidence/noise, and optimization weight are distinct quantities and should not be conflated.
human_decision_options: retain strict Task Relation Learning scope and return to causal data-regime diagnostics
explicitly broaden scope to optimization-aware multi-task learning
conservative_default: retain strict Task Relation Learning scope
